 WHO concludes the Climate and Health Co-benefits Challenge, showcasing climate solutions from around the world
 Selected case studies from 20 countries, spanning clean energy, transport, urban design and food systems, were published on ClimaHealth ahead of COP31.
 17 November 2026 
 Departmental update 
 Reading time: 
 The World Health Organization Asia-Pacific Centre for Environment and Health (WHO ACE) has concluded the Climate and Health Co-benefits Challenge , selecting 24 case studies from almost 100 cases received from around the world. Each case study highlights climate action beyond the health sector that delivers measurable benefits for health and well-being. All selected case studies are now available on ClimaHealth.
 Launched on the sidelines of the Seventy-ninth World Health Assembly in May 2026, with support from The Rockefeller Foundation and the Pathfinder Initiative, the Challenge called on governments, academic institutions, civil society, the private sector and international agencies to share real-world evidence of climate investments that are already delivering for the health and livelihoods of communities around the world.
 The Challenge set out to close a persistent gap. The health returns of climate action are real, but they remain undervalued in climate finance and policy decisions. The WHO Global Action Plan on Climate Change and Health and the Belém Health Action Plan adopted at COP30 both call for intersectoral action that maximizes these co-benefits. The selected case studies show what that looks like in practice.
 What the case studies show 
 The selected case studies span energy, transport, urban planning, food and agriculture, water and sanitation, and nature-based solutions. Together they show that when climate investments are designed with health in mind, they deliver cleaner air, cooler neighbourhoods, healthier diets and more resilient communities.
 Explore all 24 case studies on ClimaHealth From Pre-COP31 to COP31 
 A selection of submissions was previewed at Pre-COP31 in Nadi, Fiji. The full portfolio is now officially launched as world leaders gather in Antalya, Türkiye, for COP31 to accelerate implementation of the Paris Agreement. The launch at COP31 ensures evidence from the ground informs decisions at the highest level. Together, the case studies offer clear evidence that protecting the climate and protecting health go hand in hand.
   © WHO / Vincent Chen   
 COP31 is the first Conference of the Parties since the Belém Health Action Plan was adopted at COP30, with its call for intersectoral action that maximizes health and climate co-benefits. These case studies show that call is already being answered, and make the case for greater ambition, increased investment and accelerated implementation.
 Beyond COP31, the portfolio offers governments and financing partners proven models to adapt, invest in and replicate across countries and contexts. Next, WHO ACE will develop selected case studies into investment cases that can support scaling or replication in different contexts. It will also work directly with countries to explore how this evidence can help accelerate the implementation of their national climate plans.
 The solutions exist. They are already working. Now they must be taken to scale.
